messages:
alice: hey team — heads up after upgrading our app to the py SDK 1.26.x our streaming calls are silently dropping when we pass a generator/iterable as the request body. no exception on the client, stream just ends immediately.

alice: repro summary: POST /v1/stream with `body` as a generator yields no tokens. server logs show 200 but downstream consumers get empty payload. this worked on 1.25.x. not sure if it's related to the new body coercion changes.

alice: minimal snippet we use:```py
def gen_chunks():
    for i in range(3):
        yield f"chunk {i}\n".encode()

resp = client.post_stream("/v1/stream", body=gen_chunks())
for part in resp:
    print(part)
```

support-bot: ticket #15872 created and linked to this thread :ticket:

sam: thanks @alice — can you confirm exact SDK version (`pip show redwood` or `pip freeze`) + whether you're running sync or async client? also any proxies/load balancers in front?

alice: `redwood==1.26.1` (installed via pip in our CI). using sync client in Gunicorn workers behind nginx. no proxies that mutate body.

jess: hi all — SDK maintainer here. thanks for the repro. this rings a bell: 1.26 introduced a change that normalizes body types to support chunked streaming, but i think a type-check regression made plain Python iterables (not async, not file-like) get coerced to an empty bytes object in the streaming path. that would explain the silent drop.

jess: quick workaround you can do immediately: wrap generator with `itertools.chain` or an `io.BytesIO` wrapper so the SDK treats it as a file-like stream, e.g.:```py
from io import BytesIO
from itertools import chain

# wrap generator output into a file-like object
wrapped = BytesIO(b"".join(gen_chunks()))  # simple blocking workaround
resp = client.post_stream("/v1/stream", body=wrapped)
```

jess: or pin back to 1.25.4 until we cut a patch: `pip install redwood==1.25.4` — that will restore previous behavior.

alice: downgrading to 1.25.4 fixed it for our test app, confirmed. thanks.

eng-ml: noticing another related regression: the retry config rename in 1.26 seems to have changed default behavior such that some timeouts trigger an extra client retry, which caused duplicate billing for a couple of customers. not sure if it's the same change set but worth flagging.

jess: good catch — we unintentionally renamed/removed an internal idempotency check in the retry layer in 1.26 which can cause duplicate replays for non-idempotent endpoints when the streaming handshake fails. patch is in progress to restore idempotency logic + fix iterable detection. patch will target 1.26.2.

sam: escalation plan: i'll open an internal incident and assign to eng-runtime oncall, link GH issue and the reproducer. will also communicate recommended workaround (pin to 1.25.4 or use BytesIO wrapper) to affected customers. cc @eng-ml for billing impact tracking.

ci-bot: CI run for branch fix/iterable-detection passed unit tests, failing one integration test (streaming-shutdown) — will investigate.

alice: thanks all — can you ping here when 1.26.2 is published? we want to upgrade asap but can't risk silent drops or duplicate charges. :pray:

jess: definitely. i'll post the release notes and the advisory. ETA for patch rollout ~ next 24-48h assuming integration tests are green. temporary advisory we'll publish to customers: pin to 1.25.4 or apply the BytesIO wrapping workaround.

sam: added note to support KB and customer-facing alert draft. linking #15872 -> GH issue rwd/py-sdk#4921.

alice: appreciated. will monitor and hold on upgrades until we see the patch. :+1:
